# P-11 · Authorization Boundary

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Step | P Prepare (system level) |
| Phases | PH-MSA (primary) |
| Depends on | P-10 |
| Inputs | ART-INV, ART-STAKE, EXT-PRODUCT |
| Outputs | ART-BND (produces) |
| Writes facts | boundary_id |
| Minimum interviews | 1 |
| RACI | R: PER-PM, PER-ISSM · A: PER-AO · C: PER-CIO, PER-SPONSOR, PER-CISO, PER-PRIV, PER-LSE, PER-ISSE · I: — |
| Persona cards | [PER-PM](../../personas/PER-PM.md), [PER-ISSM](../../personas/PER-ISSM.md), [PER-AO](../../personas/PER-AO.md), [PER-CIO](../../personas/PER-CIO.md), [PER-SPONSOR](../../personas/PER-SPONSOR.md), [PER-CISO](../../personas/PER-CISO.md), [PER-PRIV](../../personas/PER-PRIV.md), [PER-LSE](../../personas/PER-LSE.md), [PER-ISSE](../../personas/PER-ISSE.md) |

Purpose: Determine the authorization boundary of the system, its network architecture and data flows.
<!-- END rmf:header -->
<!-- rmf:body authored -->

## Steps

1. **Entry check.** P-10 is done (`uv run rmf status <run>`), so `artifacts/data/inventory.yaml`
   exists. Why: the boundary is drawn around the assets P-10 identified.
2. **Read the inputs** in `## Inputs`. List every component the inventory names, and every
   external system, service or interconnection the product mentions.
3. **Interview** PER-ISSE, then PER-AO (`## Interviews`). The ISSE explains the
   architecture, interfaces and data flows; the AO, who is accountable for the boundary,
   confirms what is inside it and what is external.
4. **Write `artifacts/data/boundary.yaml`** from `templates/data/boundary.yaml`:
   - `authorization_boundary.description`: what is inside, what is outside, and where the
     edge is, with `sources`.
   - `network_architecture.description`: networks, interfaces, permitted traffic, with
     `sources`.
   - `data_flow.description`: each flow across or inside the boundary and how it is
     protected, with `sources`.
   - Omit `diagrams` unless a diagram file exists in the run; a listed path must exist.
   - `components`: every component inventory items point to, plus each external system or
     service the system connects to or inherits from.
     - `id`: the same `CMP-*` IDs P-10 used (and the product uses). Why: seeded allocation
       data and every inventory item refer to them (INV-BND-001).
     - `type`: an OSCAL component type (`hardware`, `software`, `service`,
       `interconnection`, ...). Never `this-system`; the CLI adds that component.
     - `status`: the component's lifecycle (`under-development` for a system not yet
       operating).
     - `external: true` for everything outside the boundary.
     - Leave `leveraged_authorization` unset; C-1 adds it once the leveraged
       authorizations are recorded.
5. **Write the boundary fact.** Rewrite `facts.yaml` whole, keeping every existing field,
   and set:

   ```yaml
   boundary_id:
     value: ESG-BND-1
     set_by_task: P-11
     sources: [INT-003.A2]
   ```

   Use `<product acronym>-BND-1` (acronym from `product/profile.yaml`) unless the AO gave
   the boundary another identifier. Why: FACTS-001 needs `set_by_task: P-11`, and the ID is
   cited by later artifacts through the facts block.
6. **Write `artifacts/ART-BND.md`** from `templates/artifacts/ART-BND.md`: the boundary
   rationale (why each external item is outside), the network architecture, and the data
   flows, each section traced. Do not restate the boundary ID; `rmf build` injects it.
7. **Build and check.** `uv run rmf build <run>`, then `uv run rmf check <run> --task P-11`,
   until 0 errors.
8. **Journal** a CHECKPOINT, and a DECISION for the AO's boundary confirmation.

## Interviews

| Persona | Why | Question focus |
|---|---|---|
| PER-ISSE | designs the security architecture (C) | interfaces and ports, permitted flows, segmentation, which components share the boundary, what the system relies on outside it |
| PER-AO | accountable for P-11 (A); DoDI 8510.01 names the AO as primary | is this the set of components the AO will authorize; are external services authorized separately; any boundary condition |
| PER-PM (optional) | responsible (R) | what the program controls and funds, which units or sites are in scope |

At least 1 interview; this playbook expects the PER-ISSE and PER-AO interviews.

## Inputs

- `artifacts/ART-INV.md`, `artifacts/data/inventory.yaml`
- `artifacts/ART-STAKE.md`
- `product/architecture.md`, `product/data-flows.md`, `product/profile.yaml`

## Outputs

| File | Front-matter | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `artifacts/data/boundary.yaml` | — | schema `boundary` |
| `artifacts/ART-BND.md` | `artifact_id: ART-BND`, `produced_by_task: P-11`, `touched_by: [P-11]` | C-1 appends itself later |
| `facts.yaml` | — | `boundary_id` only |

## Facts

| Field | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `boundary_id` | `<ACRONYM>-BND-1` or the AO's identifier | the AO's confirming answer |

## Done when

- `boundary.yaml` describes the boundary, network architecture and data flows, and lists
  every component inventory items name plus the external ones.
- `facts.yaml` has `boundary_id` with `set_by_task: P-11`.
- `uv run rmf check <run> --task P-11` reports 0 errors.

## Journal and lessons

- CHECKPOINT: `## <time> · CHECKPOINT · task P-11`, with the component counts (inside,
  external).
- DECISION: `## <time> · DECISION · task P-11 · by: PER-AO (simulated, INT-###.A#)` for the
  boundary confirmation.
- If the AO moved a component across the boundary, record why in the DECISION body.
